title: ContourGlobal Breaks Ground on Project Sterling, a large Solar-Plus-Storage Project in Arizona.
summary: Approximately 400 jobs will be created during construction of the […]
body_markdown:
- *Approximately 400 jobs will be created during construction of the* *project,* *which* *combines 509 MWp / 450 MWac of solar PV capacity with 360 MW / 1.4 GWh of battery energy storage.*
- *Sterling will serve a long-term power purchase agreement with Tesla covering more than 1 TWh of clean electricity per year* *—* *one of the largest corporate solar-plus-battery storage PPAs ever signed for a single hybrid renewable plant in the U.S., and ContourGlobal’s biggest PPA to date.*
- *ContourGlobal has secured an Equity Bridge Loan with a syndicate of leading international banks to support the project’s financing structure during construction.*


**Phoenix, Arizona, October** **7** **, 2026 —** ContourGlobal today celebrated the start of construction of Project Sterling, a hybrid solar-plus-storage facility located roughly 20 miles north of Lake Havasu City in Mohave County, Arizona. The plant will combine 509 MWp / 450 MWac of solar PV with 360 MW / 1.4 GWh of battery storage across a footprint of more than 2,000 acres in the Mojave Desert, one of the sunniest regions in the United States. Construction will continue through 2028 and involve an average of approximately 400 workers, making a tangible contribution to the local economy.


The groundbreaking ceremony was held in Topock and attended by **Antonio Cammisecra, President & CEO of ContourGlobal** , **Javier Alvarez Canedo, General Manager USA of ContourGlobal** , as well as representatives of Arizona state and local institutions, industrial partners and the community.


“ *Arizona’s sun has been shining on this land for billions of years. Project Sterling will put it to work by turning sunlight into electricity and storing part of* *that energy for delivery* *after sunset. Our teams engineered the project around the specific needs of our customer, enabling it to deliver reliable clean power for up to 16 hours a day* ,” said **Antonio Cammisecra** . “ *Today’s ceremony marks the visible beginning of our partnership with Mohave County, the State of Arizona and our customer, Tesla. We are thrilled to celebrate this milestone with them and with the people who will now build this plant safely, with respect for the local community and the land of the Mojave Desert* *.* ”


The ceremony was attended by **Jeremiah Dean** , Renewable Energy and Land Use Manager at the Arizona Governor’s Office of Resiliency; **Leo Biasiucci** , Arizona State Representative for District 30; **Ron Gould** , Vice-Chairman and Supervisor for District 5 on the Mohave County Board of Supervisors, alongside local community members, county agencies and emergency services.


Local construction teams will carry out civil works, road construction and site logistics to install more than 760,000 solar modules and over 300 battery storage containers (1.4 GWh / 360 MW) using advanced lithium iron phosphate (LFP) technology, with liquid cooling and integrated fire protection. As construction progresses, ContourGlobal will continue to work closely with Mohave County officials and local communities to ensure lasting benefits for the region.


Once operational, Sterling is expected to generate more than 1.1 TWh (terawatt-hours) of clean electricity annually—comparable to the yearly residential electricity demand of a city of 100,000 to 120,000 people—making it ContourGlobal’s largest renewable asset worldwide. The plant will serve a long-term PPA with Tesla covering around 90% of its expected output, representing one of the largest corporate solar-plus-storage PPAs ever signed for a single hybrid plant in the United States.


Project Sterling also benefits from the Western States power interconnection, reinforcing Arizona’s role in supporting a more resilient regional grid. Representatives of the Western Area Power Administration (WAPA) and the California Independent System Operator (CAISO) attended the groundbreaking event.


Sterling is a privately financed project. ContourGlobal recently secured an Equity Bridge Loan from a syndicate of leading international banks to support the project’s financing structure and the efficient deployment of capital during construction.


**A meaningful project for Arizona and ContourGlobal**


The project sits just off a historic stretch of Route 66 between Topock and Kingman, where infrastructure that once supported America’s westward expansion now gives way to infrastructure designed to power its next phase of growth. To access the site, the company is building Polaris Road, a 5.2-mile (8.4-kilometre) route connecting historic Route 66 with a project that represents a milestone in America’s power build-out.


Sterling marks another step in the pursuit of commercially viable 24/7 clean energy through large-scale solar-plus-storage projects. ContourGlobal has already begun advancing this model in Chile, where it launched one of the world’s first solar PPAs to supply electricity exclusively at night. With Project Sterling, the company is now taking another step forward by developing a plant capable of delivering clean power for up to 16 hours a day, extending well beyond sunset and enhancing grid reliability and flexibility.


ContourGlobal remains committed to growing in the United States. Following the recent completion of Black Hollow Sun in Colorado, its U.S. portfolio now totals 2.4 GW in operation or under construction. This includes 1.2 GW of thermal generation across 10 plants in California, New Mexico and Texas, as well as 1.2 GW of renewables and storage, including 324 MWp of operating solar PV and Project Sterling, which is now under construction.
